panels.rationale: H&E histology of synovial tissue from the left knee in a case report of enteropathic arthritis; caption describes inflammatory process with vascular proliferation and fibrinous exudate. It supports large-joint peripheral arthritis, but the histology is nonspecific and disease attribution relies on the disease-focused article title and case context.
panels.attribution_text: Mohamed Said et al. Etanercept in the treatment of recalcitrant enteropathic arthritis: a case report.. Journal of medical case reports 2012. doi:10.1186/1752-1947-6-10. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Synovial tissue of the left knee (hematoxylin and eosin staining, ×400). A fragment of fibrocollagenous connective tissue stroma admixed with fibrinous exudates and abundant foci of vascular proliferation indicates an inflammatory process.
in_text_mentions: e revealed 'rice bodies', which are fibrocollagenous connective tissue stroma admixed with fibrinous exudates and abundant foci of vascular proliferation, suggestive of inflammatory arthritis (Figure 1). One month after the operation, the left knee effusion recurred and there was persistent elevation of the inflammatory markers. Subsequently, a left knee arthroscopic debridement and near-total synovectomy were performed five years ago. Ten milligrams of oral methotrexate weekly was added one month after the operation, on top of 1 g of sulfasalazine twice a day, 10 mg of prednisolone once daily
